title: 江上渔者
author: 范仲淹
intro: People on the riverbank love the taste of perch — but look at the tiny boat out there, appearing and vanishing in the waves. A four-line reminder of the danger behind something delicious.
analysis: 这首诗只有二十个字，写的是江边两种人。前两句写岸上的人：江边来来往往的人，只喜欢鲈鱼味道鲜美。鲈鱼是江南有名的美食。后两句诗人请我们看江上：你看那一条小小的船（“一叶舟”，小得像一片树叶），在大风大浪里一会儿出现，一会儿又看不见了。打鱼的人冒着生命危险，岸上的人却只想到鱼好吃。前后一对比，诗人对渔民辛苦和危险的同情就表达出来了，也提醒人们：享受的时候不要忘了别人付出的代价。“出没风波里”五个字很有画面感，一个“没”字（mò，沉下去、看不见）让人替小船捏一把汗。
analysisEn: In just twenty characters this poem shows two kinds of people by a river. The first two lines are about the people on shore: crowds coming and going along the bank who care only about how tasty the perch is — perch from the lower Yangtze was a famous delicacy. Then the poet asks us to look out at the water: see that boat, small as a single leaf, appearing and disappearing among the wind and waves. The fisherman is risking his life, while the people on the bank think only of their dinner. By setting the two halves side by side, the poet shows his sympathy for the hard, dangerous work of fishermen, and reminds us not to forget what others pay for our enjoyment. The last line is very visual. The word 没 (mò, “to sink out of sight”) makes us hold our breath as the little boat vanishes behind a wave — and then reappears.
background: Fan Zhongyan (989–1052) was a Northern Song statesman, general and reformer, best remembered for his saying that one should “worry before the world worries, and rejoice after the world rejoices”. Grown up in poverty, he often wrote with concern for ordinary people.
pronunciation: 出没 chū mò（“没”读 mò，不读 méi）；君看 jūn kàn。
version: 采用通行教材版本，全诗四句，无重要异文。

lines.lit: People coming and going on the river,
lines.en: The crowds that come and go along the river

lines.lit: only love the perch’s fine taste.
lines.en: only love the taste of perch.

lines.lit: You, look at the one-leaf boat:
lines.en: But look at that boat, no bigger than a leaf,

lines.lit: appearing and sinking in the wind and waves.
lines.en: lost and found again among the wind and waves.

words.note: 者：……的人。今天说“渔民”“打鱼的人”。
现代汉语仍用，如“来来往往”“往来频繁”。
古义“只”，和今天“但是”的“但”不同；成语“但愿”还保留古义。
今天仍是名贵的食用鱼，如“清蒸鲈鱼”。
古代对人的尊称，今天说“你”“您”。

words.en: a boat as small as a leaf

words.note: 现代汉语仍用，如“野兽出没”。注意“没”读 mò。
今天多比喻纠纷、事端，如“一场风波”。

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 同一条江，岸上是热闹的人群，江心是危险的风浪，形成鲜明对比。
imagery.en: The same river holds a busy crowd on the bank and dangerous waves in the middle — a sharp contrast.

imagery.name: 鱼
imagery.zh: 鲜美的鲈鱼是岸上人的享受，也是渔民冒险的原因。
imagery.en: The delicious perch is a treat for those on shore — and the reason the fisherman risks his life.

imagery.name: 船
imagery.zh: 像树叶一样小的渔船，在风浪中忽隐忽现，写出渔民的渺小和危险。
imagery.en: A boat as small as a leaf, now seen, now gone in the waves, shows how small and exposed the fisherman is.
